newsitem.title: USA: Winnebago optimistic despite Q2 writedown.
newsitem.headline: Winnebago optimistic despite Q2 writedown.

text.p: Winnebago Industries Inc on Monday said its long-term prospects in the United States were favorable even though a writedown of selected European assets hurt its fiscal second-quarter results.

Winnebago, which makes motor homes, said it took a $5 million charge for a writedown at Winnebago Industries Europe GmbH. For its second quarter ended March 1, it posted a loss of $0.15 a share versus a profit of $0.09 for the comparable period the previous year.
The writedown was the result of excess inventory buildup and the closing of rental and retail operations at Kirkel, Germany, the company said.

"The company is refocusing this operation as a result of the continuing sluggish RV market conditions in central Europe," Winnebago Chairman and Chief Executive Fred Dohrmann said in a statement, referring to the market for RVs, or recreational vehicles.
"The long-term outlook for motor home sales domestically, however, appears very favorable," he said.
The company also said it added Bruce Hertzke and Richard Scott to its board of directors. Its bylaws were amended at the March 20 annual meeting to increase the size of the board to 10 members.
Hertzke, 45, is president and chief operating officer of Winnebago. He joined the company in 1971 and has served in various production and engineering supervisory positions.
Scott, 62, is vice president of university development at Baylor University in Waco, Texas.
